page: Amazon Web Services c6g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a 64-bit ARM architecture powered by an AWS Graviton processor using Neoverse-N1 cores. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 24286.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8581.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 969.0 and a weak rating in single-threaded gzip compression. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached small blocks at 946.86 GB/sec, but drops to 169.7 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The ARMv8 architecture supports hardware-accelerated AES cryptography, though it lacks AVX or AMX instruction sets. Database operations and web serving are solid, with Redis SET operations reaching 19.74 million operations per second and static web serving throughput averaging 18.73 GB/sec.

The c6g.4xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. Because it utilizes custom ARM silicon, it delivers competitive resource density and compute capabilities per unit of cost compared to traditional x86 architectures. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations. However, it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks, heavy cryptographic operations, or large-scale LLM inference, where its performance falls into the weak or poor categories.
